text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Seventy-five youths and street kids in the capital appear in court charged with rioting.
- Former President Kenneth Kaunda demands that the November 1996 presidential elections be nullified and a fresh poll be called this year.
- Peace returns to Lusaka after a spate of riots by street vendors.
- Former president Kenneth Kaunda says the government is deliberatley fanning civil unrest to enable it declare a state of emergency and ban his party.
- Suspended high court judge Kabazo Chanda resigns from the judiciary, saying he cannot work with "intellectually bankrupt buffoons and perverts".
